B-r1.title: Mammoth Steak: a bone-in bison rib steak, reverse-seared and carved at the table

B-r2.title: Mammoth Steak (bone-in bison, reverse-seared, carved at the table)

B-r4.title: Mammoth Steak (bone-in, reverse-seared, carved at the table)

notes.b1/j1/B-r1: Thorough reverse-sear bison rib with honest mammoth sourcing (permafrost meat, lab-grown meatball) and an ice-age table, though it runs long and gets clinical.
notes.b1/j1/A-r1: Clean, compact bison reverse sear with an honest opener, but mammoth is barely present beyond the juniper and a stock 'ice age' nod.
notes.b1/j1/B-r2: Most mammoth-literate (Yuka, dogs eating carcasses, Yakutian horse, reindeer swap) with a carve-at-the-table show, but heavy on caveats and sections.
notes.b1/j1/A-r2: Generic pan-seared steak with a one-line mammoth disclaimer and inconsistent oven/timing instructions.
notes.b1/j2/B-r2: Very rigorous, honest reverse-sear with real mammoth facts, but long and padded with sourcing and safety sections.
notes.b1/j2/A-r2: Competent generic ribeye recipe with a one-line extinction caveat and almost no mammoth world.
notes.b1/j2/A-r1: Clean, concise reverse sear with a tidy honest note and juniper, but little mammoth texture.
notes.b1/j2/B-r1: Best blend of mammoth lore, tundra table staging and precise method, though somewhat long.
notes.b1/j3/A-r2: Competent generic bison steak with a one-line mammoth disclaimer and almost no mammoth world.
notes.b1/j3/B-r2: Rich, honest sourcing (Yuka, permits, dogs eating carcasses), carve-at-table showpiece and thorough method, though long and a bit heavy on caveats.
notes.b1/j3/B-r1: Same strong research as X (lab-grown mammoth meatball, permafrost fry) plus a tundra-table serving scene, rye, lingonberry and a leftovers plan; tighter and more playful.
notes.b1/j3/A-r1: Concise, clean recipe with a nice extinct-4000-years note and 'very ice age' juniper, but otherwise a standard game steak.
notes.b2/j1/B-r3: Rigorous, honest sourcing and a show-cut reverse sear, but long and more steak manual than mammoth play.
notes.b2/j1/A-r3: Competent but generic steak with a muddled premise about cooking a real mammoth cut and a stray 'check for parasites' note.
notes.b2/j1/B-r4: Mammoth-as-size-and-story tomahawk carved at table, thorough times and temps, honest about sourcing, though a bit padded.
notes.b2/j1/A-r4: Clean concise recipe with a juniper pan sauce but treats mammoth as a beef steak with only a nod to the animal.
notes.b2/j2/B-r4: Thorough, honest reverse-sear tomahawk with real permafrost and permit facts, but long and the mammoth is only a size gag.
notes.b2/j2/A-r4: Clean, concise pan-seared steak with juniper sauce; competent but generic, and calls mammoth close to elephant lean red meat with little else.
notes.b2/j2/A-r3: Treats real mammoth meat as an option and gives hot-and-fast advice for tough old meat, which is muddled and inconsistent.
notes.b2/j2/B-r3: Show-plate framing with Yakutia horse and reindeer stand-ins, sourcing options and scaling table, but heavy with extras and padding.
notes.b2/j3/A-r4: Clean, honest, compact stand-in recipe with a juniper wine sauce, but little mammoth world beyond a one-line nod.
notes.b2/j3/B-r4: Thorough bone-in reverse-sear with real permafrost and permit detail, but long with troubleshooting and gamey-fix padding.
notes.b2/j3/B-r3: Show-plate framing with Yakutia horse and reindeer and carved-at-table drama; most mammoth-aware but overlong with scaling tables.
notes.b2/j3/A-r3: Treats extinct meat as legitimate then hedges; ingredients list mammoth steaks and advice is muddled, though lingonberry and braise tips are nice.
